#### The Structures of the Biquaternion Algebra

<a href="articles_maths/classification-of-the-structures-of-the-biquaternion-algebra.html">Classification of the Structures of the Biquaternion Algebra</a>
<!-- the two notions that change the ground field, the real structure as a conjugate-linear multiplicative involution of the complex algebra with its real form the fixed set, the complex structure as a unital map of $\mathbb{C}$ into the centre of the real algebra equivalently a central $J$ with $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$, and the statement that the two questions run in opposite directions and are not inverse, both halving the real dimension; the classification of the real structures, exactly two up to isomorphism because the central simple algebras of real dimension four are $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathbb{H}$, with the compact one the coefficient conjugation $\sigma_{\mathrm{comp}}(\tilde Q)=\overline{\tilde Q}$ of fixed set the quaternion subspace $\mathbb{B}_H=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{e_t,\vec e_x,\vec e_y,\vec e_z\}$ a division algebra, and the split one the inner twist $\sigma_{\mathrm{split}}(\tilde Q)=-\vec e_y\overline{\tilde Q}\vec e_y$ of fixed set $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{e_t,\vec e_y,i\vec e_x,i\vec e_z\}$ which is $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ in the Pauli dictionary, with the action on the base, the closure of the span, the halving of the real dimension, and the identification of the four images $\mathrm{I}_2,\ \sigma_1,\ -i\sigma_2,\ \sigma_3$; the separation of the two by one element, the idempotent $\tfrac12(e_t+i\vec e_x)$ and the zero divisor $P(e_t-P)=0$ in the split form and the absence of both in the division form; the corollary on the inner twists $\operatorname{Ad}_u\circ\sigma_{\mathrm{comp}}$ for a unit $u$ with $u\bar u$ central, the class decided by the sign of $u\bar u$, negative giving the real matrices and positive giving the quaternions, with the two witnesses $\vec e_y$ and $i\vec e_x$, and the remark that an inner twist is not a conjugacy of the forms because a conjugate-linear fixed equation is twisted unless $u\bar u=+e_t$; the counting of the two structures of $\mathbb{C}$ against the one complex form; the unique complex structure, given by multiplication by $i e_t$, and the separation of the complex form $\mathbb{B}$ of complex dimension four from the complexification $M_2(\mathbb{C})\oplus M_2(\mathbb{C})$ of complex dimension eight; the six remarkable subspaces read against the structures, the compact fixed set one of the six and the split fixed set not one of them, the complex structure preserving the centre and the vector subspace and exchanging the quaternion with the anti-quaternion and the Hermitian with the anti-Hermitian, and the reason $\mathbb{B}_{\Psi}$ is not a real form, the involution ${}^{*}$ being an anti-automorphism; the Lie dictionary of the two structures, $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ as the traceless part of the quaternion fixed set with Killing form $(-,-,-)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ as the traceless part of the real matrices with inertia $(2,1)$, together with $\mathfrak{u}(1)$, $\mathfrak{u}(2)$, $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{R})$, $\mathfrak{so}(3,1)$ and $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}$ with their dimensions, simply connected groups and inertias; and what the structures do not decide, the four products and their forms, the six subspaces, the subalgebras and the topology, the group being fixed only up to the choice of a discrete central subgroup. The forms of the four products are *The Four Forms and the Four Algebraic Norms over the Biquaternion Algebra*, the subspaces are *Subspaces and Decompositions of the Biquaternion Algebra*, the group theory is *Biquaternion Lie Group and Exponential Structure* and *Biquaternion Rotations and Lorentz Transformations*, the general theory of the two operations is *Real Forms and the Descent of an Algebra*, the theorem on the two real forms of the matrix algebra is *The Split Real Form: $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ inside $M_n(\mathbb{C})$*, and the discrete central subgroups are *The Lie Correspondence and the Adjoint Representation*. -->

the Killing forms, $K(X,Y)=4\operatorname{tr}(XY)-2\operatorname{tr}X\operatorname{tr}Y$ on each factor, the scalar line isotropic and orthogonal to everything, the restriction to the traceless part equal to four times the trace form, the table of ranks with radical two on the sum and one on the Borel, and the warning that the inertia is not a complex invariant, the two inertias $(2,1)$ and $(3,0)$ of $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{C})$ being those of its two real forms; the real-form lattice, the theorem that a real structure on the sum preserves or exchanges the two simple summands, the four preserving ones with fixed algebras $\mathbb{H}\oplus\mathbb{H}$, $\mathbb{H}\oplus M_2(\mathbb{R})$, $M_2(\mathbb{R})\oplus\mathbb{H}$, $M_2(\mathbb{R})\oplus M_2(\mathbb{R})$ and the one exchanging class with fixed algebra $M_2(\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}$, five structures and four algebras, the correction of the four-item list that omits the mixed pair and counts the slanted form twice, and the diagonal correspondence $x\mapsto(x,\bar x)$ from each real form of $\mathbb{B}$ into its own pair form and into the slanted form with the commutation of the two real structures as its proof; the involutions, the coefficient conjugation, the quaternion conjugation, the star and the transpose with fixed spaces of dimensions four, two, four and six, the six remarkable subspaces of dimensions $2,6,4,4,4,4$, and the intersection table $1,3,4,0,1,3$ whose fourth column is the compact column of the companion article; the Lie groups, the correspondence cited once, the centres $\{\pm I\}$, $(\mathbb{Z}/2)\times\mathbb{C}$, $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{C}$ of the covers, the worked entry for $\mathfrak{gl}(2,\mathbb{C})$ through the covering $SL(2,\mathbb{C})\times\mathbb{C}\to GL(2,\mathbb{C})$ of kernel $\langle(-I,\pi i)\rangle$ and fundamental group $\mathbb{Z}$, the worked entry for $\mathfrak b_0$ through $\widetilde{B^+}=\mathbb{C}^3$ of centre $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{C}$ and the group $B^+$ of fundamental group $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the master table of eight rows, and the warning that the centre of the cover is not the centre of the group; the comparison of the two articles in one table and the three differences read as one difference, the splitting into two ideals, the two-dimensional centre and the closure under square roots; what the complex form determines, the factors, the centre, the lattices, the four families and the Killing ranks, and what it does not, the real form, the inertia, the position of the real subspaces, the discrete central subgroup and the unitary representation theory, with the closing warning box; and the hand-off to the real article, the structure article, the operator series and the Lie correspondence. The two real forms are *Classification of the Real Structures of the Biquaternion Algebra, including Lie Algebras and Lie Groups*, the ground-field structures are *Classification of the Structures of the Biquaternion Algebra*, the six subspaces are *Subspaces and Decompositions of the Biquaternion Algebra*, the Peirce cut is *Peirce Decompositions of the Biquaternion Algebra*, the group theory is *The Lie Correspondence and the Adjoint Representation*, the inertias are *The Killing Form of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and Its Three Inertias*, the two real forms of the matrix algebra are *Real Forms and the Descent of an Algebra* and *The Split Real Form: $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ inside $M_n(\mathbb{C})$*, and the operator level is the operator series. -->

the theorem that $M_4(\mathbb{C})$ has exactly two real forms, the split $M_4(\mathbb{R})$ and the quaternionic $M_2(\mathbb{H})$, by Wedderburn and Frobenius at dimension sixteen, obtained as the fixed sets of the entrywise and the quaternionic conjugation and separated by the inertias $(10,6)$ and $(6,10)$ of the trace form; the real forms $L(\mathbb{H})$ and $L(M_2(\mathbb{R}))$ of the regular families, the images of the six remarkable subspaces with the same dimensions and the same statuses, two subalgebras, two Lie subalgebras and two that are neither; the Jordan layer as a third lattice with the real forms $M_4(\mathbb{R})^{+}$, $M_2(\mathbb{H})^{+}$ and the Hermitian $H_4(\mathbb{C})$, which has no associative real form above it, and the shadow $L(\mathbb{B}_{\Psi})\subset H_4(\mathbb{C})$ of the observables; and the relation to the element level, the two embeddings $\iota_L$ and $\iota_R$ of dimension four, which do not classify, the two-sided span $\mathcal{E}(A_0)\cong A_0\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}A_0^{\mathrm{op}}$, which gives $M_4(\mathbb{R})$ for both element-level real forms, so that the compact element-level form generates the split operator-level form and the passage is not injective, the two spans distinct and conjugate with an eight-dimensional intersection, the witness $R_{\vec e_x}$ fixed by the induced compact structure and carried to $-R_{\vec e_x}$ by the split one, and the quaternionic operator form $\mathcal{E}^{\mathbb{H}}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{H}}(\mathbb{B})\cong M_2(\mathbb{H})$, selected by the module structure and not by the subalgebra, with $\mathcal{E}^{\mathbb{H}}\cap\mathcal{E}_{\mathbb{C}}=L(\mathbb{B})$; <a href="articles_maths/the-spin-one-carrier-and-the-rank-strata.html">The Spin-One Carrier and the Rank Strata</a>

### Topology

#### Introduction to Topology on the Biquaternions

<a href="articles_maths/topology-in-the-space-of-biquaternions.html">Topology in the Space of Biquaternions</a>
<!-- the topology of the space of biquaternions, built from the linear structure alone and with no form and no algebraic norm entering: a **norm** defined by the three axioms (real-valued, non-negative, definite, homogeneous, subadditive) and the norm $\lVert\tilde Q\rVert=(\sum_\mu\lvert Q_\mu\rvert^{2})^{1/2}$ of the real space $\mathbb{B}=\mathbb{R}\text{-span}\{e_\mu,ie_\mu\}\cong\mathbb{R}^{8}$; **the theorem of finite dimension** — every two norms on a finite-dimensional real space are equivalent, and such a space carries exactly one Hausdorff vector-space topology — whence **one topological norm** and one topology (Rudin 1.21–1.22, Bourbaki I, *Normed and Banach Spaces*, *Comparison of Norms and Invertibility*); **the construction** of the topology: the metric $d(\tilde Q_2,\tilde Q)=\lVert\tilde Q_2-\tilde Q\rVert$, the balls, the coordinate isomorphism and the arrival at the **Euclidean topology of $\mathbb{R}^{8}$**, with the usual properties (Hausdorff, second countable, locally compact, complete, path connected, Heine–Borel) and the subspace topology from the regular representation into $M_4(\mathbb{R})$; then the algebra structure in it — the product bound $\lVert\tilde Q_2\tilde Q\rVert\leq\sqrt2\lVert\tilde Q_2\rVert\lVert\tilde Q\rVert$, proved from $\lVert\mathsf{M}_2(\tilde Q)\rVert_F=\sqrt2\lVert\tilde Q\rVert$ and the Frobenius norm, so that $\mathbb{B}$ is a topological, normed and Banach algebra and its group of invertibles is open. This is the only article of the introduction to topology: the topology does not depend on the forms. -->

#### Topology of the Biquaternion Algebra

<a href="articles_maths/the-euclidean-topology-of-the-biquaternion-algebra.html">The Euclidean Topology of the Biquaternion Algebra</a>
<!-- the Euclidean structure of the ambient space, independent of the forms: the real inner product and the Euclidean norm, which is the topological norm, the linear isometry onto $\mathbb{R}^8$; the sharp normed-algebra inequality $\lVert\tilde Q\tilde Q_3\rVert\le\sqrt2\lVert\tilde Q\rVert\lVert\tilde Q_3\rVert$; the contractibility with $\pi_n(\mathbb{B})=0$ and the contractibility of the remarkable subspaces; the Euclidean unit sphere $S^7$, not a group and meeting the null cone in the compact $5$-manifold link; the Riesz duality and the flat Riemannian metric. Moved into this region out of the former parked region, where it sat under a heading that named a topology for a form. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-biquaternion-group-of-invertibles-as-a-topological-group.html">The Biquaternion Group of Invertibles as a Topological Group</a>
<!-- $\mathbb{B}^\times$ with its group structure and its topology, open and dense as the complement of the null cone; the determinant and the matrix model $GL_2(\mathbb{C})$; the retraction of $\mathbb{B}^\times$ onto its maximal compact subgroup; the retraction of the determinant-one group; the structure of the maximal compact subgroup; the homotopy groups, the generators and the universal cover; the connected components. This is the topological part of the Lie-theoretic block, which the boundary places in three parts: the Lie algebra in *Symmetric and Antisymmetric Decomposition of the Four General Products*, the topology here, the Lie-group theory in *Biquaternion Lie Group and Exponential Structure*. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-topology-of-the-zero-divisor-cone.html">The Topology of the Zero-Divisor Cone</a>
<!-- the null cone of the algebraic norm as a topological object, built with no form entering beyond the Euclidean norm that defines the unit sphere: the null cone $\mathcal{N}=\{N=0\}$, closed with empty interior, a complex cone of real dimension $6$, with the group of invertibles as its open and dense complement; the punctured cone $\mathcal Z=\mathcal{N}\setminus\{0\}$ as a smooth complex $3$-manifold of which the apex is the only singular point; the contractibility of the cone by $\tilde Q\mapsto(1-s)\tilde Q$; the link $L=\mathcal{N}\cap S^7_E$ as a closed connected real $5$-manifold, identified as $L\cong S^2\times S^3$, equivalently an $S^1$-bundle over the projectivised cone $S^2\times S^2$, with $\pi_1=0$, $\pi_2\cong\mathbb{Z}$ and $\pi_3\cong\mathbb{Z}\oplus\mathbb{Z}$, so not $S^5$, which certifies the apex as genuinely singular; the two definite planes of the pure subspace, which the cone meets only at the apex and whose unit spheres are the spheres of real roots of $-1$ and $+1$; and the Lorentzian slices, on which the cone cuts a three-dimensional null cone with link $S^2\sqcup S^2$. The algebraic norm is *The Four Forms and the Four Algebraic Norms over the Biquaternion Algebra*; the criterion and the strata are *N-Regularity and N-Degeneracy in the Biquaternion Algebra*; the ambient Euclidean structure and the unit sphere are *The Euclidean Topology of the Biquaternion Algebra*; the projective geometry of the cone's complex lines is not treated; the article carries the form-free half of the former *Biquaternion Topology*. -->

### Analysis

#### General Analysis

<a href="articles_maths/biquaternion-analysis.html">Biquaternion Analysis</a>
<!-- the Euclidean norm and the metric structure of $\mathbb{B}$; the distance, balls and neighbourhoods; limits of functions and continuity; the problem of differentiability and its two obstructions, the failure of left and right division and the zero divisors; the standard approach and the function theory it defines; functions on a four-dimensional subspace and their partial derivatives; the biquaternionic gradient and its quaternion conjugate; the d'Alembertian, the square of the gradient and the convective derivative; the relation to Fueter and Clifford analysis. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-first-order-root-of-the-biquaternion-d-alembertian.html">The First-Order Root of the Biquaternion D'Alembertian</a>
<!-- the d'Alembertian $\Box=\langle\tilde\nabla\rangle_{\natural}=\mathrm{Sc}(\tilde\nabla^{\natural}\tilde\nabla)=\partial^2/\partial Q_t^2+\Delta_Q$ as the norm of the gradient and the question of its first-order root; the biquaternion algebra is $M_2(\mathbb{C})$, and the $M_4(\mathbb{C})$ below is the enveloping operator algebra of the regular module, not a second representation; the two senses, the single square $D^2=(\Box-\lambda)I$ and the factorisation $D_-D_+=(\Box-\lambda)I$; the root condition on $D=\sum_\mu\gamma^\mu\partial/\partial Q_\mu+B$, the Clifford relation $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\delta^{\mu\nu}I$, the anticommutator $\{\gamma^\mu,B\}=0$ and the square $B^2=-\lambda I$; the complex Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}_4(\mathbb{C})\cong M_4(\mathbb{C})$, the sixteen monomials, the minimal carrier $\mathbb{C}^4$ and the uniqueness up to similarity; the three generators $\gamma_k=i\vec e_k$ inside $\mathbb{B}$, the no-go for a fourth left multiplication and the failure of the two-dimensional simple module; the regular module $\mathbb{B}=S_+\oplus S_-$, the two minimal left ideals, the exchange $u=\vec\Pi_{\mathrm{nil},+-}+\vec\Pi_{\mathrm{nil},-+}$ with $u^2=e_t$, the grading $G=R_{\tilde\Pi_+}-R_{\tilde\Pi_-}$ with $R_uG=-GR_u$, the two-sided generators $\gamma^t=R_u$ and $\gamma^k=L_{\gamma_k}G$, the frame $\gamma^t=\sigma_1\otimes I_2$, $\gamma^k=\sigma_3\otimes\gamma_k$, $\gamma_5=\sigma_2\otimes I_2$, written as operators $\gamma^t=T_{e_t,u}$, $\gamma^k=T_{\gamma_k,\tilde\Pi_+}-T_{\gamma_k,\tilde\Pi_-}$, $\gamma_5=iT_{e_t,\vec\Pi_{\mathrm{nil},+-}}-iT_{e_t,\vec\Pi_{\mathrm{nil},-+}}$, and the generation of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$ by the two-sided algebra; the unshifted root $\mathsf D$ with $\mathsf D^2=\Box I$; the shifted operator, the pseudoscalar shift $\mathsf D_\lambda=\mathsf D+c\gamma_5$ with $c^2=-\lambda$, the converse, the scalar shift and the factorisation $(\mathsf D-\kappa)(\mathsf D+\kappa)=\Box-\kappa^2$; the chiral form, the two rows $D_+\psi_+=c\psi_-$ and $D_-\psi_-=-c\psi_+$, the chiral half of the kernel, the spectral projectors of the scalar factorisation and the full kernel; the determinant $\det\mathsf D_\lambda=(\Box-\lambda)^2$ and its agreement with $\det\mathsf M_4(\tilde\nabla)=\Box^2$; the classification of carriers and the freedom of the frame; worked examples. ### Geometry

<a href="articles_maths/biquaternion-rotations-and-lorentz-transformations.html">Biquaternion Rotations and Lorentz Transformations</a>
<!-- the geometry of the isometric motions: the unit sphere $Sp(1)$ and its complexification $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$, the Lorentz rotors; the double covers $SL(2,\mathbb{C})\to SO^+(1,3)$ and $SU(2)\to SO(3)$, with the dimension count that excludes a six-dimensional group from the four-dimensional quaternions and places the double cover in the eight-dimensional algebra, the group itself in the projective complement of the null quadric; the rotor and the two-sided action, the half-angle and the doubling of the angle; the bilinear two-sided operator $\mathrm{H}_{\tilde Q}(x)=\tilde Qx\tilde Q^{*}$ on the whole algebra, with the reason the conjugate and not the inverse is the right factor; the orbits and the invariants, the rank and the norm scaled by $\lvert N(\tilde Q)\rvert^{2}$; the two-sided action and $SO(4)$; the boosts, or hyperbolic rotations, as the isometries of the indefinite form and the rotations as those of the definite one. The reflection $\rho_v(x)=-vxv^{-1}$ with $N(v)=1$ on the Clifford vector subspace, the anticommutation criterion and the Cartan–Dieudonné generation are stated here; the general statement is *Versors, Rotors and the Two-Sided Action with Signed Inner Conjugation* and *The Clifford, Pin and Spin Groups with Signed Inner Conjugation* of Part II, cited and not restated. The operator theory of the bilinear two-sided operator — composition, factorisation through the polar word, the scaling of the norm, the kernel $U(1)$, the image $CO^+(1,3)$ and the infinitesimal form — is *Two-Sided Operators on the N-Regular Sector*; the action on the six remarkable subspaces, the table of preserved subspaces and the theorem on the elements whose two-sided operator preserves all of them are *The Complete Polar Decomposition and Remarkable Subspaces*; nothing of those articles is reproved here. The representation theory of these groups — the group of invertibles, the finite-dimensional representations of the Lorentz group, the Weyl and Dirac spinors, the Clebsch–Gordan rule and the principal series — is carried in the same article. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-biquaternion-quadratic-map-and-its-julia-sets.html">The Biquaternion Quadratic Map and Its Julia Sets</a>
<!-- the iteration of $z\mapsto z^2+c$ in the biquaternion algebra, an eight-real-dimensional non-commutative and non-division setting; the several inequivalent readings of the square, the product, the left and right products and the matrix product, and the choice of the map which each defines; the Julia set as the boundary of the bounded orbit locus, defined off the zero divisors and studied through the matrix model; the standing caveat that no choice is canonical, which is what separates this theory from the complex and the quaternion cases. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-slices-of-the-biquaternion-julia-sets.html">The Slices of the Biquaternion Julia Sets</a>

<a href="articles_maths/the-escape-radius-and-the-greens-function-for-the-biquaternions.html">The Escape Radius and the Green's Function for the Biquaternions</a>
<!-- the escape radius of the biquaternion quadratic map and the difficulty it meets, since the norm is not multiplicative on a non-division algebra and the zero divisors allow a product to collapse; the Green's function as the limit of the normalised logarithmic potential of the iterates, together with the domain on which the limit exists; the Monge–Ampère current and the equilibrium measure, conditional on the regular part because the pullback loses mass at the cone; the comparison with the complex and the quaternion cases, where the radius is controlled by the multiplicative norm; the point at which the escape theory of this category genuinely departs from the classical one. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-zero-divisors-and-the-singular-julia-sets.html">The Zero Divisors and the Singular Julia Sets</a>

<a href="articles_maths/the-matrix-element-representation-and-the-biquaternion-dynamics.html">The Matrix Element Representation and the Biquaternion Dynamics</a>

<a href="articles_maths/the-idempotent-decomposition-and-the-split-fractal-of-the-biquaternions.html">The Idempotent Decomposition and the Split Fractal of the Biquaternions</a>
<!-- the central idempotents of the biquaternion algebra and the decomposition of an element into two halves, each carrying the dynamics of a quaternion or a complex algebra; the split fractal obtained by iterating the two halves independently, and the reconstruction of the biquaternion fractal from the pair; the cases in which the pair commutes, so the split is clean, and the cases in which it does not; the contrast with the split-biquaternion decomposition, where the idempotents act differently. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-biquaternion-iterated-function-systems.html">The Biquaternion Iterated Function Systems</a>

## The Matrix Algebras $M_n(\mathbb{R})$

<!-- the real matrices before the complex ones: the same spine, over the base field where the involution does not produce a positive definite form and where the antisymmetric half is a Lie algebra. Two things exist here and nowhere over $\mathbb{C}$: exactly two conjugacy classes of involutions of the first kind, the transpose and the symplectic, whose fixed spaces have the same dimension $n(n+1)/2$ but one is a Jordan algebra and the other a Lie algebra; and a spectrum that is not contained in the base field, so the Jordan form carries rotation blocks and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ has two components. The trace form is indefinite, of inertia $(n(n+1)/2,\,n(n-1)/2)$, so no form of this algebra is both invariant and definite. The entries marked NEW are planned and not yet written; each becomes an anchor line with its own comment when the article exists. -->

<!-- the killing form $\operatorname{K}(X,Y)=2n\operatorname{tr}(XY)-2\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb{R})$; its radical equal to the centre $\mathbb{R}\mathrm{I}$ and its restriction to $\mathfrak{sl}_n(\mathbb{R})$ equal to $2n$ times the trace form, of inertia $\bigl(n(n+1)/2-1,\,n(n-1)/2\bigr)$ measured as $(2,1),(5,3),(9,6)$ at $n=2,3,4$; the killing form on $\mathfrak{so}(n)$, negative definite with eigenvalues $-2,-2,-2$ at $n=3$ and $-4$ six times at $n=4$, and vanishing at $n=2$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-four-forms-and-their-algebraic-norms-over-r.html">The Four Forms and Their Algebraic Norms over $\mathbb{R}$</a>

#### The Idempotents and the Peirce Decomposition

<a href="articles_maths/lagrange-idempotents-of-a-real-matrix-with-simple-real-spectrum.html">Lagrange Idempotents of a Real Matrix with Simple Real Spectrum</a>
<!-- the $n$ canonical idempotents $P_k=\prod_{l\ne k}(A-\lambda_l\mathrm{I})/(\lambda_k-\lambda_l)$ of a real matrix with $n$ distinct real eigenvalues; the identities $P_kP_l=\delta_{kl}P_k$, $\sum_kP_k=\mathrm{I}$ and $A=\sum_k\lambda_kP_k$; the idempotents as the spectral projections and their lagrange interpolation reading; the failure of the construction at a repeated or a nonreal eigenvalue, and the two-conjugate-pair replacement. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-peirce-decomposition-in-n-dimensions-over-r.html">The Peirce Decomposition in $n$ Dimensions over $\mathbb{R}$</a>
<!-- a frame of $n$ orthogonal idempotents cutting $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ into the $n^{2}$ corners $A_{kl}=P_kM_n(\mathbb{R})P_l$ of dimension $r_kr_l$; the multiplication rule $A_{kl}A_{lm}\subseteq A_{km}$ with $A_{kl}A_{mn}=0$ for $l\ne m$; the diagonal corners as the endomorphism algebras $M_{r_k}(\mathbb{R})$ and the off-diagonal ones as the homomorphism spaces; the abstract peirce identities verified on random elements. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-peirce-basis-and-the-corners-over-r.html">The Peirce Basis and the Corners over $\mathbb{R}$</a>
<!-- a real frame cutting $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ into $n^{2}$ corners that multiply by the matrix-unit table; the matrix units $E_{kl}$ of a frame, their product rule and the dimension $r_kr_l$ of each corner; the residual frame group, conjugation by an invertible real matrix, and the dimension $n^{2}-n$ of the frame variety; the systems of matrix units of the real algebra and the reconstruction of the algebra from one of them. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-peirce-decomposition-of-sym-n-r-as-a-jordan-algebra.html">The Peirce Decomposition of $\operatorname{Sym}_n(\mathbb{R})$ as a Jordan Algebra</a>
<!-- a real orthogonal projection $E$ cutting $\operatorname{Sym}_n$ into three peirce spaces of dimensions $r(r+1)/2$, $r(n-r)$ and $(n-r)(n-r+1)/2$, summing to $n(n+1)/2$; the jordan product $\tfrac12(XY+YX)$ and its peirce rules $V_{ii}\circ V_{ii}\subseteq V_{ii}$, $V_{ii}\circ V_{ij}\subseteq V_{ij}$ and $V_{ij}\circ V_{ij}\subseteq V_{ii}+V_{jj}$; the formally real structure and the cone as the set of squares; the case $r=1$ written explicitly. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-peirce-decomposition-and-the-two-halves-over-r.html">The Peirce Decomposition and the Two Halves over $\mathbb{R}$</a>
<!-- the transpose sending the corner $A_{kl}$ onto $A_{lk}$, so each corner pair splits into a symmetric and an antisymmetric part of equal dimension; the grading of the two halves of $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ by the frame; the corners as the graded pieces and the two projections $\pi_{\pm}$ read on each pair; the conservation of the dimension count $n(n+1)/2$ and $n(n-1)/2$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/spinors-as-peirce-coordinates-over-the-reals.html">Spinors as Peirce Coordinates over the Reals</a>
<!-- the off-diagonal peirce coordinates of a real matrix as maps between the lines of a frame; the case $n=2$ where the two off-diagonal coordinates are a pair of real numbers exchanged by the transpose; the action of the frame group on the pair and the two invariants; the comparison with the complex case, where the pair is a spinor and its conjugate, and the limit of the real reading. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-peirce-decomposition-and-the-corner-recursion-of-mnr.html">The Peirce Decomposition and the Corner Recursion of $M_n(\mathbb{R})$</a>
<!-- one real idempotent of rank $r$ cutting $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ into four corners of dimensions $r^{2}$, $r(n-r)$, $(n-r)r$ and $(n-r)^{2}$; the recursion that the corner algebra contains $M_r(\mathbb{R})$ and $M_{n-r}(\mathbb{R})$ with two bimodules between them; the peirce rules $x_{ij}x_{kl}=\delta_{jk}x_{il}$ for $i,j,k,l\in\{1,2\}$; the descent to $r=1$ and the recovery of the full frame by iteration, with the dimension count verified. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-frame-the-simple-nilpotents-and-the-real-frame-group-of-mnr.html">The Frame, the Simple Nilpotents and the Real Frame Group of $M_n(\mathbb{R})$</a>
<!-- a complete real frame carrying $N=\sum_kc_kE_{k,k+1}$ with all $c_k\ne0$, the simple nilpotents, whose coefficients live in $n-1$ copies of $\mathbb{R}^{\times}$; the frame group of the frame, the diagonal rescalings and the space of frames with $2^{n-1}$ components; the relations $NE_{k,k+1}=0$ and $E_{k,k+1}N$ between the nilpotent and the idempotents; the canonical form of the pair and the checks at $n=3,4$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-spectral-theorem-the-symmetric-case.html">The Spectral Theorem: the Symmetric Case</a>
<!-- every real symmetric matrix as $S=Q\Lambda Q^{\mathsf T}$ with $Q$ orthogonal and $\Lambda$ real diagonal, with an orthonormal basis of real eigenvectors; the proof by the real schur form, where symmetry forces every rotation block to be a scalar; the variational reading through the rayleigh quotient and the min-max characterisation; the spectral projections and the peirce idempotents of the symmetric algebra. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-spectral-theorem-the-antisymmetric-case-and-the-purely-imaginary-spectrum.html">The Spectral Theorem: the Antisymmetric Case and the Purely Imaginary Spectrum</a>
<!-- every real antisymmetric matrix as a direct sum of planar rotations together with zeros, with a purely imaginary spectrum; the parity argument forcing a zero block at odd $n$; the canonical form $Q\,\mathrm{diag}(0,\dots,0,\theta_1J,\dots,\theta_mJ)\,Q^{\mathsf T}$ and the angles defined up to order and sign; the pfaffian at even $n$ and the determinant as a square. -->

## The Matrix Algebras $M_n(\mathbb{C})$

### Algebra

<a href="articles_maths/the-elementary-symmetric-functions-and-det-i-plus-ta.html">The Elementary Symmetric Functions and $\det(\mathrm{I}+tA)$</a>
<!-- the sum of the principal $k\times k$ minors and its identification with the elementary symmetric functions of the eigenvalues; the expansion $\det(\mathrm{I}+tA)=\sum_ke_kt^{k}$ proved by the Leibniz rule, and its form as the characteristic polynomial; the invariance of the polynomial across $AB$ and $BA$; Newton's identities and the power sums; the invariant ring generated by the $e_k$ with degrees summing to $n(n+1)/2$; Jacobi's formula, the derivative $\operatorname{tr}A$ and $\det e^{A}=e^{\operatorname{tr}A}$; the two coefficients at $n=2$ and the fact that the biquaternion norm is not the determinant. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-minimal-polynomial-and-the-jordan-form.html">The Minimal Polynomial and the Jordan Form</a>
<!-- the annihilator of $A$ and its monic generator, of degree at most $n$ by Cayley–Hamilton; the identity of the roots of the minimal and the characteristic polynomial, with exponents the sizes of the largest blocks; the Jordan form and the uniqueness of its list; the classification by Jordan type and the open orbit of the nonderogatory matrices; the dimension of the centraliser as the sum of the squares of the conjugate partition, checked on the nilpotents of size at most four; the partition numbers $2,3,5,7,11$ for $n=2,\dots,6$; the three kinds at $n=2$ and the companion nilpotent. -->

#### Involutions, Flags, and the Decompositions

<a href="articles_maths/the-involutions-over-r-and-over-c.html">The Involutions over $\mathbb{R}$ and over $\mathbb{C}$</a>
<!-- the automorphism and the anti-automorphism of order two, the first kind linear and the second antilinear; the classification of the reversing linear involutions as the transpose and, for even $n$, the symplectic transpose, with the invariant $S^{\mathsf T}=\pm S$; the $n+1$ inner involutions by $\operatorname{diag}(\mathrm{I}_p,-\mathrm{I}_{n-p})$ and their fixed algebra $M_p\oplus M_{n-p}$; the $n+1$ Hermitian structures indexed by inertia and the two real structures; the split $\tfrac12(\mathrm{I}\pm\sigma)$ and the dimensions $n(n+1)/2$ and $n(n-1)/2$, exchanged by the symplectic involution; the exchange $UT_n^{\mathsf T}=LT_n$ and the diagonal as the only fixed part there. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-over-r-symmetric-and-antisymmetric.html">The Two Halves over $\mathbb{R}$: Symmetric and Antisymmetric</a>
<!-- the split $A=\tfrac12(A+A^{\mathsf T})+\tfrac12(A-A^{\mathsf T})$ and the dimensions $n(n+1)/2$ against $n(n-1)/2$ summing to $n^{2}$; the orthogonality of the halves for the trace form; the symmetric half as a Jordan algebra under the anticommutator, with real spectrum and orthogonal diagonalisation; the antisymmetric half as $\mathfrak{so}(n)$, of rank $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with even rank, purely imaginary spectrum and $\det K=\operatorname{Pf}(K)^{2}$; the closure rules across the halves; the Killing form $(n-2)\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ degenerate at $n=2$; the two exponentials, rotations and positive stretches. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-over-c-hermitian-and-anti-hermitian.html">The Two Halves over $\mathbb{C}$: Hermitian and Anti-Hermitian</a>
<!-- the split $A=\tfrac12(A+A^{*})+\tfrac12(A-A^{*})$ into two real subspaces of dimension $n^{2}$ each and the exchange by multiplication by $i$; the Hermitian half as a real Jordan algebra with real spectrum and unitary diagonalisation; the anti-Hermitian half as $\mathfrak{u}(n)$ and its traceless part $\mathfrak{su}(n)$, with purely imaginary spectrum; the orthogonality for the real part of the trace form only, and the inertias $(n^{2},0)$ and $(0,n^{2})$ of the bilinear form; the exponentials to $\mathrm{U}(n)$ and to the positive cone; the Pauli basis at $n=2$ and the mixed corners that leave both halves. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-fine-decomposition-against-the-diagonal.html">The Fine Decomposition against the Diagonal</a>
<!-- the diagonal subalgebra of dimension $n$ as a maximal torus and the grading of the algebra into $n^{2}$ one-dimensional weight lines $\mathbb{C}E_{ij}$ with weight $t_i/t_j$; the roots $\epsilon_i-\epsilon_j$ of the system $A_{n-1}$, $n(n-1)$ in number and $n(n-1)/2$ positive, the positive ones indexing the pairs; the simple roots and the simple nilpotents $E_{k,k+1}$; the reversal of the weight by the transpose and the split of each pair into $E_{ij}+E_{ji}$ and $E_{ij}-E_{ji}$, whence the two halves as coarsenings; the identity of the Peirce lines with the weight lines at the coordinate flag; the case $n=2$ and the biquaternion frame. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-as-orthogonal-complements.html">The Two Halves as Orthogonal Complements</a>
<!-- the lemma that the two eigenspaces of an involution preserving a form are orthogonal for it, with the two-line proof; the real case, $M_n(\mathbb{R})=\operatorname{Sym}_n\perp\operatorname{Skew}_n$ for $\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}C)$, with the dimension count giving $\operatorname{Sym}_n^{\perp}=\operatorname{Skew}_n$ and the inertias $(n(n+1)/2,0)$ and $(0,n(n-1)/2)$; the complex case, $\operatorname{Herm}_n\perp\operatorname{SkewHerm}_n$ for the real part of the Hilbert–Schmidt form, with the purely imaginary cross term; the matrix units as an orthonormal system and the fine decomposition as an orthogonal one; the orthogonal projections $\tfrac12(\mathrm{I}\pm\sigma)$; the failure of complementarity when the form is not preserved. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-triangular-decomposition-h-n-plus-n-minus.html">The Triangular Decomposition $h\oplus n_+\oplus n_-$</a>
<!-- the direct sum $M_n=\mathfrak{h}\oplus n_+\oplus n_-$ with dimensions $n$, $n(n-1)/2$, $n(n-1)/2$, and the three summands as the weight-zero and the two signs of the roots; the nilpotency of $n_+$ with index exactly $n$ and the derived algebra $[n_+,n_+]=\operatorname{span}\{E_{ij}:j-i\ge2\}$ of dimension $(n-1)(n-2)/2$; the solvable Borel $\mathfrak{b}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus n_+$ of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with $[\mathfrak{b},\mathfrak{b}]=n_+$; the bracket $[n_+,n_-]$ larger than the diagonal, of dimension $13$ at $n=4$; the mutual orthogonality of the three summands for $\operatorname{tr}(A^{\mathsf T}C)$; the $LDU$ reading and the open Bruhat cell. -->

<a href="articles_maths/utn-as-the-complement-of-the-antisymmetric-part-transpose-case.html">$UT_n$ as the Complement of the Antisymmetric Part (Transpose Case)</a>
<!-- the direct sum $M_n(\mathbb{R})=UT_n\oplus\operatorname{Skew}_n$ with dimensions $n(n+1)/2$ and $n(n-1)/2$, and the symmetric half as the other complement of the same dimension, the only one that is the annihilator; the projection $\pi(A)=\operatorname{strict}(A)-\operatorname{strict}(A)^{\mathsf T}$ along the triangular algebra, idempotent with kernel $UT_n$, and its difference from the orthogonal projection $\tfrac12(A-A^{\mathsf T})$; the failure of $\pi$ to be a Peirce projection $A\mapsto eA$, of the image to be an ideal, and of the half to contain an idempotent; the failure of $[\operatorname{Skew}_n,UT_n]\subseteq UT_n$, so the decomposition is not a symmetric pair; the reading at $n=2$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/symmetric-pairs-and-cartan-pairs-the-reductivity-criterion.html">Symmetric Pairs and Cartan Pairs: the Reductivity Criterion</a>
<!-- the involution $\theta(X)=-X^{\mathsf T}$ as an automorphism of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ with $\mathfrak{k}=\mathfrak{so}(n)$ and $\mathfrak{p}=\operatorname{Sym}_n$ and the three bracket rules; the reductivity criterion $[\mathfrak{k},\mathfrak{p}]\subseteq\mathfrak{p}$ with its two-line proof, as the exact test for a complement to be the anti-fixed part of an involution; the symmetric half passing and $UT_n$ failing, with the diagonal as the obstruction; the Cartan pair and the definiteness of $B_\theta(X,Y)=-B(X,\theta Y)$, the Killing form $2n\operatorname{tr}(XY)-2\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ and $2n\operatorname{tr}(XX^{\mathsf T})>0$ on $\mathfrak{sl}_n$; the case $n=2$. -->

#### The Spectrum

<a href="articles_maths/the-spectrum-of-a-matrix.html">The Spectrum of a Matrix</a>

<a href="articles_maths/the-spin-one-carrier-of-mnc.html">The Spin-One Carrier of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$: the Three-Dimensional $V_1$</a>

<!-- the $n$ carriers against $n^{2}$ complex and $2n^{2}$ real dimensions; the linear closure as the carrier itself and the multiplicative closure as $1$ or $n^{2}$; the table for $n=2$ to $6$; the spin $n-1=2j$; why the four real-form closure rules of the biquaternion article have no general-$n$ analogue. -->

### Topology

<a href="articles_maths/the-topology-of-mnc.html">The Topology of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- the matrix space as a real Euclidean space of dimension $2n^2$, contractible, complete and locally compact, with the Hilbert–Schmidt norm as the norm of the coordinates and the equivalence $\|A\|_2\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\sqrt n\|A\|_2$; the determinant as a polynomial, so $\mathrm{GL}_n$ is open, dense and not closed with boundary the singular set; the singular set as a complex hypersurface of real codimension two, hence of measure zero and thin, and the path connectedness of the group; the rank strata as closed sets, the exact-rank stratum of dimension $2nr-r^2$ and the orbit of codimension $2(n-r)^2$; the contraction to the apex, the retraction onto the unitary group and the division of the Hermitian half into the regions of constant inertia; the case $n=2$ with the seven-dimensional cone of rank at most one. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-and-their-topology.html">The Two Halves and Their Topology</a>
<!-- the two halves as real vector spaces of dimension $n^2$, closed and meeting only at $0$, each homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{n^2}$; the splitting map $\Phi(A)=(\tfrac12(A+A^{*}),\tfrac12(A-A^{*}))$ as a linear homeomorphism and the Pythagorean identity $\|A\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2=\|H\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2+\|K\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2$ with the involution as an isometry; the Hermitian half cut by the inertia into $n+1$ open connected regions separated by the singular set, the rank strata of dimension $2nr-r^2$; the positive cone as open and convex, contractible to $\mathrm{I}$ and homeomorphic to the half through the exponential; the unitary group compact of dimension $n^2$ and not contractible because of the surjection $\det:\mathrm{U}(n)\to S^1$; the case $n=2$ with three Hermitian regions and the circle bundle over $S^3$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-space-of-idempotents-and-the-flag-varieties.html">The Space of Idempotents and the Flag Varieties</a>
<!-- the idempotents as the splittings $V=\operatorname{im}e\oplus\ker e$, with $\operatorname{tr}e=\operatorname{rank}e$ and the complement $\mathrm{I}-e$; the stratification by the rank, the transitive action of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ with the Levi stabiliser and the complex dimension $2k(n-k)$; the tangent equation $\delta=\delta e+e\delta$ and the four corner blocks; the Hermitian idempotents as the orthogonal projections, the Grassmannian $\mathrm{U}(n)/(\mathrm{U}(k)\times\mathrm{U}(n-k))$ of real dimension $2k(n-k)$ and its Hermitian off-diagonal tangent directions; the complete sets of idempotents as flags, the flag variety of real dimension $n(n-1)$, the Lagrange idempotents and the partial flags of complex dimension $\sum_j d_j(d_{j+1}-d_j)$; the case $n=2$ with the two-sphere of rank one projections and the pair $\tilde\Pi_\pm$ as a diameter. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-homotopy-of-glnc-and-of-the-two-halves.html">The Homotopy of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and of the Two Halves</a>
<!-- the polar retraction $r(A)=(AA^{*})^{-1/2}A$ onto $\mathrm{U}(n)$, the homeomorphism $\mathrm{GL}_n\cong\mathrm{U}(n)\times\mathrm{PD}_n$ and the vanishing of $\pi_0$; the surjection $\det:\mathrm{U}(n)\to S^1$, the loop $\gamma(t)=e^{2\pi it}\mathrm{I}$ of winding $n$, and $\pi_1(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C}))=\mathbb{Z}$ with $\pi_k=\pi_k(\mathrm{SU}(n))$ for $k\ge2$; the two components of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{R})$; the covering $\mathrm{SU}(n)\times S^1\to\mathrm{U}(n)$, the simple connectedness of $\mathrm{SU}(n)$ and $\pi_3=\mathbb{Z}$; the contractibility of both halves and of the cone, so the split is invisible to the homotopy; the case $n=2$ with $\pi_1=\pi_3=\mathbb{Z}$ and the two signs of the rotor as two sheets of a covering. -->

### Analysis

<a href="articles_maths/the-analysis-on-mnc.html">The Analysis on $M_n(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- the space as a unital noncommutative Banach algebra with $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\rho(A)\le\|A\|$ and the zero divisors of the nilpotents; the $C^*$-identity $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, the antimultiplicative isometric involution and the order by the spectrum; the power series on a disc containing the spectrum, the holomorphic functional calculus, the spectral mapping theorem and the logarithm near the identity; the derivatives $D\det(A)H=\det(A)\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}H)$, $D\,\mathrm{inv}(A)H=-A^{-1}HA^{-1}$, $D\exp(A)H=\int_0^1e^{sA}He^{(1-s)A}ds$ and $D\operatorname{tr}=\operatorname{tr}$; the smooth structure of the space and of the open group of dimension $2n^2$, with $D\exp(0)=\mathrm{id}$; the case $n=2$ with the functional calculus on the two Peirce coordinates and the logarithm near $e_t$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-exponential-and-the-lie-group-structure.html">The Exponential and the Lie Group Structure</a>
<!-- the commutator, the Jacobi identity, the derived algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_n$, the centre $\mathbb{C}\mathrm{I}$ and the split $\mathfrak{gl}_n=\mathfrak{sl}_n\oplus\mathbb{C}\mathrm{I}$; the group as a Lie group of real dimension $2n^2$ with that algebra; the exponential as a local diffeomorphism with $D\exp(0)=\mathrm{id}$ and the logarithm as local inverse, with the resonances $\lambda_i-\lambda_j\in2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$; the surjectivity over $\mathbb{C}$, the periods $2\pi ik\mathrm{I}$ and the failure of injectivity, the image of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ onto $\mathrm{SL}_n$; the one-parameter subgroups as the exponentials, the two halves as rotations and stretches; the adjoint action $\operatorname{Ad}_g(X)=gXg^{-1}$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{e^X}=e^{\operatorname{ad}_X}$, and the Campbell–Baker–Hausdorff formula beginning $X+Y+\tfrac12[X,Y]$; the case $n=2$ with the three-dimensional traceless part and the corner curves. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-positive-cone-and-its-boundary.html">The Positive Cone and Its Boundary</a>
<!-- the cone $\mathrm{PD}_n$ as an open convex pointed subset of the Hermitian half of real dimension $n^2$ with closure the positive semidefinite matrices; the self-duality $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\ge0$ for the trace form and the roundness of the cone; the boundary as the singular matrices, the faces $F_W$ indexed by the subspaces with $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}F_W=(\dim W)^2$ and the minimal face of an element given by its image; the extremal rays $\lambda vv^*$ and the rank one characterisation; the transitivity of $\mathrm{GL}_n$, the stabiliser $\mathrm{U}(n)$ with $\mathrm{PD}_n=\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})/\mathrm{U}(n)$, the congruences up to scalars and the involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$; the concavity of $\log\det$, the vanishing on the boundary and the level sets as the orbits of $\mathrm{SL}_n$; the case $n=2$ with the hyperbolic base and the corner values. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-and-the-analysis-smooth-structures-and-the-exponential.html">The Two Halves and the Analysis: Smooth Structures and the Exponential</a>
<!-- the projectors $\pi_{\mathrm{H}}$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{S}}$ as real-linear contractions of norm one, self-adjoint and anti-self-adjoint for the Hilbert–Schmidt form, and the split with $\dim_{\mathbb{R}}=n^2+n^2$; the halves as flat smooth submanifolds and Banach subspaces with tangent space equal to themselves, and the adjoint as the involution whose fixed and anti-fixed sets are the halves; the exponential on the Hermitian half as a diffeomorphism onto the cone with the logarithm as inverse and the spectral image $\operatorname{Spec}(e^A)=e^{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}$; the exponential on the anti-Hermitian half as a surjection onto $\mathrm{U}(n)$ with the period lattice $\operatorname{Spec}\subset2\pi i\mathbb{Z}$, hence never injective; the polar decomposition from the two charts and its uniqueness up to the lattice; the case $n=2$ with the corner values real and imaginary. -->

<!-- the trace metric $g_A(H,K)=\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}HA^{-1}K)$ as the second derivative of $\log\det$, its invariance under $A\mapsto gAg^*$ and its agreement with the trace form at the identity; the geodesics $A^{1/2}e^{tA^{-1/2}HA^{-1/2}}A^{1/2}$ of constant speed and the distance $\|\log(A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2})\|_{\mathrm{F}}$, invariant under the two-sided action; the nonpositive sectional curvature recomputed at $n=2,3,4$, vanishing exactly on the planes through the scalars, the formula $K=-\tfrac14\|[H,K]\|^2$, constant $-1/2$ on the traceless part at $n=2$ and variable at $n\ge3$; the definite Ad-invariant form $-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ of the anti-Hermitian half; the isometries as the two-sided operators $L_gR_{g^*}$ with isometry group $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})/\mathrm{U}(1)$ and the cone as $\mathrm{GL}_n/\mathrm{U}(n)$; the case $n=2$ with the hyperbolic three-space times a line and the corner metric. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-cone-of-positive-semidefinite-matrices.html">The Cone of Positive Semidefinite Matrices</a>
<!-- the closed convex pointed cone $\overline{\mathrm{PD}}_n$ as the closure of $\exp(\operatorname{Herm}_n)$ and as the set of the Hermitian squares; the Löwner order $A\le B\iff B-A\ge0$, compatible with the addition and the positive scalars, with the identity as order unit and the Archimedean property, and with the monotone trace; the compact convex base $\mathcal{B}_n=\{\operatorname{tr}A=1\}$ of dimension $n^2-1$, the cone over its base, and the density matrices; the extreme points as the rank one projections forming $\mathbb{CP}^{n-1}$ of dimension $2(n-1)$, and the base as their convex hull with the rank stratification $2k(n-k)$; the order preserved by the congruences, reversed by the inversion, and not preserved by the square (the explicit pair $\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ and $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$) nor by the exponential, though $e^A\le e^B$ forces $A\le B$; the case $n=2$ as the Bloch ball with the two-sphere of the pure states. -->

<!-- the biquaternion algebra $\mathbb{B}=\mathbb{C}\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{H}\cong M_2(\mathbb{C})$ of real dimension eight, its element with the trace, the determinant and the characteristic polynomial of the left multiplication, and the rank in $\{0,1,2\}$; the quaternion conjugation cutting the centre and the vector part of dimensions $2$ and $6$, the Hermitian conjugation cutting the sectors $\mathbb{B}_H$ and $\mathbb{B}_\Phi$ of four real dimensions each with the forms of inertia $(1,3)$ and $(3,1)$; the commutator $[\mathbb{B}_H,\mathbb{B}_H]\subset\mathbb{B}_\Phi$ and the adjoint action, the anti-Hermitian half as $\mathfrak{u}(2)$; the forms at two with the trace form of inertia $(4,4)$ and the two halves definite, the Killing form of rank six, inertia $(3,3)$ and radical $\mathbb{C}e_t$; the frame from a pure root $\vec{Ζ}$, the idempotents $\tilde\Pi_\pm$, the corners $\mathbb{B}_{st}$, the companion nilpotents with $uv=\tilde\Pi_+$ and the one reciprocal rescaling; the doubled spectrum, the real spectrum of the Hermitian sector, the exponential into the rotations and the stretches with the two rotor signs; the algebraic norm $N=\alpha_+\alpha_-$ on the diagonal subalgebra, of inertia $(2,2)$ there and $(4,4)$ on the whole algebra. -->

### The Five Categories

<!-- the five categories that follow instantiate the construction at $n=2,3,4,5,6$, in that order. Each repeats the spine with the data of its $n$, and adds the arithmetic of that dimension: the corner recursion, the singular set, the spectral strata. -->
## $M_2(\mathbb{C})$

<!-- the base case $n=2$, laid out on the spine of the general category and not on the layout of the instantiated ones. The subsections repeat those of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ in the same order, and each article is the $n=2$ statement of the general one. What the dimension adds is the arithmetic of two: two real forms, a characteristic polynomial of degree two, an antisymmetric half that is one line and therefore abelian, exactly one rotation plane, and a trace form of inertia $(3,1)$ on the real matrices. The entries marked NEW are planned and not yet written. -->

the Jordan layer as a third lattice with the real forms $M_4(\mathbb{R})^{+}$, $M_2(\mathbb{H})^{+}$ and the Hermitian $H_4(\mathbb{C})$, which has no associative real form above it, and the shadow $L(\mathbb{B}_{\Psi})\subset H_4(\mathbb{C})$ of the observables; and the relation to the element level, the two embeddings $\iota_L$ and $\iota_R$ of dimension four, which do not classify, the two-sided span $\mathcal{E}(A_0)\cong A_0\otimes_{\mathbb{R}}A_0^{\mathrm{op}}$, which gives $M_4(\mathbb{R})$ for both element-level real forms, so that the compact element-level form generates the split operator-level form and the passage is not injective, the two spans distinct and conjugate with an eight-dimensional intersection, the witness $R_{\vec e_x}$ fixed by the induced compact structure and carried to $-R_{\vec e_x}$ by the split one, and the quaternionic operator form $\mathcal{E}^{\mathbb{H}}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb{H}}(\mathbb{B})\cong M_2(\mathbb{H})$, selected by the module structure and not by the subalgebra, with $\mathcal{E}^{\mathbb{H}}\cap\mathcal{E}_{\mathbb{C}}=L(\mathbb{B})$; with the three corrections of the source paper, the real forms named for a real algebra, the count of the Lie-algebra forms and the complexification read as a complex form, and the closing statement of what the operator-level structures determine and do not. <!-- the product restricted to the two halves as four tables, each split into a symmetric and an antisymmetric part according to the parity of the factors; the diagonal tables spanning the whole algebra and the mixed ones the traceless algebra, of dimensions $16$ and $15$; the failure of closure exhibited by three explicit pairs of units; the two mixed tables as transposes of one another up to sign and as different maps with the same image; the four as the unsigned blocks of the multiplication in the grading by parity, the four general products of the biquaternion algebra being the signed combinations; and the axis-free frame, where the transpose is the quaternion conjugation. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-jordan-algebra-sym-4.html">The Jordan Algebra $\operatorname{Sym}_4$</a>
<!-- the symmetrised product making $\operatorname{Sym}_4$ a Jordan algebra, commutative with unit, power associative and satisfying the Jordan identity by the associativity of the ambient algebra; rank and degree four, the idempotents the orthogonal projections and the rank-$k$ ones the Grassmannian; the trace form as the restriction of the trace pairing, associative for the circle product and positive definite over $\mathbb{R}$; the determinant and the trace of the ambient algebra as the Jordan determinant and trace; the cone of squares over $\mathbb{R}$ as the cone of positive semidefinite matrices, stratified by rank; and speciality and formal reality, with the contrast over $\mathbb{C}$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-lie-algebra-skew-4-and-so-4.html">The Lie Algebra $\operatorname{Skew}_4\cong\mathfrak{so}(4)$</a>
<!-- the antisymmetric matrices as a six-dimensional Lie algebra isomorphic to $\mathfrak{so}(4)$ and to the two-forms on four-space, with the trace pairing negative definite and the Pfaffian as the square root of the determinant; the split into two three-dimensional ideals at order four, each a copy of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, given by the self-dual and the anti-self-dual forms, commuting and orthogonal for the Killing form $8\operatorname{tr}(XY)$; the two ideals carrying the two independent invariants and the two angles; the axis-free frame, where they are the spans of the left and of the right multiplications by the three vector units; and the exponential onto $\mathrm{SO}(4,\mathbb{C})$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-lie-algebra-gl4c-and-sl4c-of-m4c.html">The Lie Algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_4(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbb{C})$ of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- the bracket $[A,B]=AB-BA$ on the sixteen dimensions; the centre $\mathbb{C}I$ and the decomposition $\mathfrak{gl}_4=\mathfrak{sl}_4\oplus\mathbb{C}I$; $\mathfrak{sl}_4$ of dimension $15$, simple of type $A_3$; the Cartan subalgebra of traceless diagonal matrices, the twelve roots $\pm(\epsilon_i-\epsilon_j)$ and the root spaces $\mathbb{C}E_{ij}$; the Killing form $8\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{sl}_4$ and $8\operatorname{tr}(XY)-2\operatorname{tr}X\operatorname{tr}Y$ on $\mathfrak{gl}_4$, degenerate on the centre; the five real forms $\mathfrak{su}(4)$, $\mathfrak{su}(1,3)$, $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)$, $\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbb{R})$ and $\mathfrak{su}^{*}(4)$ with their dimensions, maximal compact subalgebras and inertias; the subalgebras $\mathfrak{so}(4)\cong\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ of the antisymmetric sector and the two Peirce $\mathfrak{su}_2$'s. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-derivation-commutator-and-its-anti-self-adjointness-for-the-trace-form-at-n-4.html">The Derivation $X\mapsto[A,X]$ and Its Anti-Self-Adjointness for the Trace Form at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the commutator map as a derivation for every element, the representation property by the Jacobi identity and every derivation inner, so that the derivations form $\mathfrak{sl}_4$ of dimension $15$; anti-self-adjointness for the trace pairing for every $A$ by the cyclic invariance of the trace; anti-self-adjointness for the Hilbert–Schmidt form exactly when $A$ is anti-Hermitian up to a real scalar, that is when the derivation lies in $\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak{u}(4)$; the difference as the involution and not the derivation, with the invariance of the trace form under all of $\mathrm{GL}_4$ against that of the Hilbert–Schmidt form under $U(4)$; and the spectrum of $\operatorname{ad}_A$ as the sixteen differences of eigenvalues, with the centraliser as kernel. -->

<!-- the derivations of the algebra, $\operatorname{Der}(M_4)=\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak{sl}_4$ of dimension $15$ and the theorem that every derivation is inner; the kernel $\mathbb{C}I$ of $\operatorname{ad}$ and the dimension count; the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(M_4)=PGL_4(\mathbb{C})$, all automorphisms inner by Skolem–Noether, with no outer automorphism; the $*$-automorphisms $PU(4)$ and the real derivations $\mathfrak{u}(4)$ of the involution; the complex-antilinear automorphisms and the coset $\operatorname{Aut}_\mathbb{R}/\operatorname{Aut}_\mathbb{C}\cong\mathbb{Z}/2$; the comparison with $\operatorname{Der}(\mathbb{B})=\operatorname{ad}\mathbb{B}$ of complex dimension $3$, and the place of the biquaternion derivations inside the fifteen. -->

<a href="articles_maths/ut4-as-a-linear-model-of-sym-4-same-space-wrong-product.html">$UT_4$ as a Linear Model of $\operatorname{Sym}_4$: Same Space, Wrong Product</a>

<a href="articles_maths/the-trace-form-and-its-inertia-on-the-two-halves-of-m4c.html">The Trace Form and Its Inertia on the Two Halves of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>

<!-- the trace form and the Frobenius, operator and nuclear norms; the determinant and the singular set $\{\det=0\}$ of real codimension two; the rank stratification and the dimension of each stratum; the absence of a null cone, the form being definite; the comparison with the cone of $\mathbb{B}$ and with its link. -->

<!-- the real-linear embedding $\mathsf{M}_4:\mathbb{B}\to\mathrm{Cl}^+(1,3)$ with $\mathsf{M}_4(i)=i\gamma^5$; the vector trace $\operatorname{Tr}_\Delta(b)=\operatorname{tr}\mathsf{M}_4(b)=4\operatorname{Re}b_0$ and the axial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Delta,\gamma^5}(b)=\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^5\mathsf{M}_4(b))=4i\operatorname{Im}b_0$; the identity $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{reg}}=\operatorname{Tr}_\Delta+\operatorname{Tr}_{\Delta,\gamma^5}$ with $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm{reg}}=4b_0$; the chiral traces $2b_0$ and $2\bar b_0$; the two coordinates of the two-sided basis, $\operatorname{tr}T_{\mu\nu}=4\delta_{\mu t}\delta_{\nu t}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^5T_{\mu\nu})=4i\delta_{\mu t}\delta_{\nu z}$, so the vector trace reads $T_{tt}$ and the axial trace reads $T_{tz}$; the vanishing on the odd sector; the pair the anomaly needs against the regular trace. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-numerical-range-and-the-field-of-values-of-m4c.html">The Numerical Range and the Field of Values of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>

<a href="articles_maths/normal-matrices-and-the-common-spectral-theorem-at-n-4.html">Normal Matrices and the Common Spectral Theorem at $n=4$</a>
<!-- normality $A^{\ast}A=AA^{\ast}$ as equivalent to unitary diagonalisability and to the vanishing of the strict upper part of the Schur form; the four matrices $A$, $A^{\ast}$, $A^{\mathsf T}$ and $\bar A$ diagonalised by the pair $U$, $\bar U$, with $A^{\mathsf T}=\bar U\Lambda\bar U^{\ast}$ and $\bar A=\bar U\bar\Lambda\bar U^{\ast}$, and one unitary sufficient when the eigenbasis is closed under conjugation; the four spectral families as the normal matrices with spectrum on the real line, the imaginary line, the unit circle and the positive half-line; the Jordan block of size four as the extreme failure, with a flag of length four; and the axis-free frame, where the left matrix of a real element satisfies $L^{\mathsf T}L=N\mathrm I_4$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-law-of-the-module-and-the-chain-of-carriers.html">The Law of the Module and the Chain of Carriers at Every $n$</a>
<!-- the law: the module is $V_{(n-1)/2}$ and the algebra is $\bigoplus_{k=0}^{n-1}V_k$ with $\sum_k(2k+1)=n^{2}$; the check at $n=2$, $3+1=4$; at $n=3$, $5+3+1=9$; at $n=4$, $7+5+3+1=16$; the faithfulness of the module exactly at even $n$, where $2j$ is odd; the odd rows, where the module's label is an integer and the module is a carrier of the algebra; and the reading that the biquaternion series cannot be continued by adding $\tfrac32$ as a fourth carrier of $\mathbb{B}$, since $\tfrac32$ labels the module of $M_4$ and not a summand of any algebra. -->

### Topology

<a href="articles_maths/the-topology-of-m4c.html">The Topology of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- $M_4(\mathbb{C})\cong\mathbb{R}^{32}$ contractible; $GL_4(\mathbb{C})\simeq U(4)$; $\pi_1=\mathbb{Z}$ and $\pi_2=0$; the space of idempotents of rank $p$ homotopy equivalent to $\operatorname{Gr}(p,4)$; the flag variety simply connected; the determinant bundle and its first Chern class. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-and-their-topology-at-n-4.html">The Two Halves and Their Topology at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the split of the complex matrix space into the Hermitian and the anti-Hermitian halves of real dimension sixteen, as the eigenspace decomposition of the adjoint involution; the singular set of each half as a hypersurface, the zero set of the determinant; the five components of the invertible real symmetric matrices indexed by inertia, grouped three and two by the sign of the determinant, and the two components of the invertible real antisymmetric matrices indexed by the sign of the Pfaffian; each class as a homogeneous space of the general linear group; and the contraction by the polar decomposition, $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{C})\simeq U(4)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{R})\simeq O(4)$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-space-of-idempotents-and-the-flag-varieties-at-n-4.html">The Space of Idempotents and the Flag Varieties at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the idempotents of rank $k$ as the projections onto $k$-planes, forming $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{4})=\mathrm{GL}_4/P_k$ of complex dimension $k(4-k)$, three for $k=1$ and $k=3$, four for $k=2$, a point for $k=0$ and $k=4$; the full flag of complex dimension six as $\mathrm{GL}_4/B$; the Hermitian idempotents as the orthogonal projections and the same Grassmannians through $U(4)$, of real dimension $2k(4-k)$ inside $\operatorname{Herm}_4$; the Peirce pair as complementary points plus the mixed blocks; and $\mathrm{Gr}_2$ as the Klein quadric in $\mathbb{P}^{5}$, with the Plücker relation as its single equation and the two rulings as the two families of planes. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-homotopy-of-gl4c-and-of-the-two-halves.html">The Homotopy of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{C})$ and of the Two Halves at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the polar decomposition making $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{C})$ homotopy equivalent to $U(4)$, which is $S^{1}\times SU(4)$ up to homotopy; the low homotopy groups, a point in degree zero, $\mathbb{Z}$ in degrees one and three and zero in degree two; $SU(4)$ simply connected of dimension fifteen, with $\pi_4=\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $\pi_5=\mathbb{Z}$; the Hermitian space and both positive cones contractible, so that the whole topology sits in the unitary part; the quotient by the unitary group contractible as the cone of positive definite matrices, against the quotient by the orthogonal group with infinite cyclic fundamental group; and the compact form inside the complex group deciding the topology of the quotient. -->

### Analysis

<a href="articles_maths/analysis-on-m4c.html">Analysis on $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- the smooth structure of $\mathbb{C}^{16}$; the derivatives of the product, the inverse, the determinant and the exponential; the Wirtinger calculus; the holomorphic functional calculus; the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^{16}$; the absence of zero divisors and the ordinary matrix analysis it gives; the boundary against Fueter theory, which needs another structure. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-exponential-and-the-lie-group-structure-at-n-4.html">The Exponential and the Lie Group Structure at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the exponential series converging everywhere, giving an invertible matrix of determinant $e^{\operatorname{tr}A}$ and homomorphic on commuting arguments; its surjectivity onto $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{C})$, every nonzero complex number having a logarithm and the logarithm of a Jordan block terminating, and over $\mathbb{R}$ only onto the positive-determinant component; the differential at the origin as the identity, with the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff correction to the addition; the one-parameter subgroups as the solutions of $\dot X=AX$; the axis-free eigenvalues $Q_t\pm iB$ twice each, so that the determinant of the exponential is $e^{4Q_t}$ and the rotor is the exponential of a bivector; and the exponential as a diffeomorphism on the Hermitian half. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-positive-cone-and-its-boundary-at-n-4.html">The Positive Cone and Its Boundary at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the positive definite Hermitian matrices as an open convex cone of real dimension sixteen, homogeneous under congruence, self-dual for the Hilbert–Schmidt form and equal to the set of squares $B^{\ast}B$ of invertible matrices; its closure as the positive semidefinite matrices, defining the Loewner order; the boundary stratified by rank with dimensions $15$, $12$, $7$ and $0$; the faces indexed by subspaces with dimension $(4-\dim W)^{2}$, the extremal rays parametrised by $\mathbb{P}^{3}$; the concavity of the logarithm of the determinant and the trace as a positive linear functional with compact sections; and the automorphism group, with stabiliser $U(4)$ of the identity and interior $\mathrm{GL}_4/U(4)$. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-two-halves-and-the-analysis-smooth-structures-and-the-exponential-at-n-4.html">The Two Halves and the Analysis: Smooth Structures and the Exponential at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the two halves as linear subspaces of real dimension sixteen, complementary at every point and each its own tangent space; the exponential a diffeomorphism from the Hermitian half onto the open cone and a surjection with discrete fibres from the anti-Hermitian half onto the unitary group; the analyticity of $A\mapsto A^{\ast}$, $\operatorname{tr}$, $\det$ and $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, with derivatives $B^{\ast}$, $\operatorname{tr}B$, $\det(A)\operatorname{tr}(A^{-1}B)$ and $-A^{-1}BA^{-1}$; $A\mapsto A^{\ast}A$ as a submersion onto the Hermitian half with the unitary orbits as fibres; the polar decomposition as a global analytic diffeomorphism onto the product; and the Jordan structure as the algebraic shadow of the analysis on the symmetric half. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-polar-decomposition-of-m4c-in-exponential-coordinates.html">The Polar Decomposition of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$ in Exponential Coordinates</a>
<!-- every invertible $A=e^{H}e^{iK}$ with $H,K$ Hermitian; the relation to the polar decomposition $A=UP$; the uniqueness and the reach of the exponential on the singular elements; the comparison with the split case. -->

### Geometry

<a href="articles_maths/the-geometry-of-the-idempotents-of-m4c.html">The Geometry of the Idempotents of $M_4(\mathbb{C})$</a>
<!-- the idempotents of rank one as an affine bundle of rank $3$ over $\mathbb{P}^{3}$, of dimension $6$; the idempotents of rank $p$ as the homogeneous space $PGL_4/P(GL_p\times GL_{4-p})$ of dimension $2p(4-p)$, a fibre bundle over $\operatorname{Gr}(p,4)$ with the contractible fibre of complements; the full flag variety $GL_4/B$ of dimension $6$; the partial flags and the incidence relations; the frame group as the fibre of the frame bundle. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-geometry-of-the-two-halves-at-n-4-and-the-return-of-the-two-sided-operators.html">The Geometry of the Two Halves at $n=4$, and the Return of the Two-Sided Operators</a>
<!-- the Hermitian half as a real space of dimension sixteen carrying the open convex self-dual cone, and the anti-Hermitian half as the Lie algebra of the unitary group; the Hermitian idempotents of rank $k$ as the Grassmannians of real dimension $2k(4-k)$ inside the Hermitian half, with the cone stratified by the same flags; $\mathrm{GL}_4/U(4)$ as a symmetric space of noncompact type of dimension sixteen, contractible, of nonpositive curvature and with the invariant trace metric, its compact dual replacing the cone by the compact section; and the return to the operators, the two-sided products giving the coordinates, the signed permutations the finite skeleton of order $32$, the trace pairing the inertia $(10,6)$, the Segre cone the rank-one part and the length the measure of the coefficient matrix. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-symmetric-space-gl4-o4-and-its-complex-twin.html">The Symmetric Space $\mathrm{GL}_4/O(4)$ and Its Complex Twin</a>
<!-- the transpose as a Cartan involution of $\mathfrak{gl}_4$ with fixed set $\mathfrak{so}(4)$ and $(-1)$-eigenspace $\operatorname{Sym}_4$, of dimensions $6$ and $10$ over $\mathbb{R}$ and again over $\mathbb{C}$; the quotient by the orthogonal group as the open cone of positive definite symmetric matrices, of rank four, with Weyl group of order $384$, nonpositive curvature and contractible topology; the complex twin as the space of nondegenerate complex symmetric forms of complex dimension ten, not contractible because the positivity is gone; the compact dual $U(4)/O(4)$ of dimension ten, with nonnegative curvature and closed geodesics; and the axis-free basis, where the ten symmetric directions are exactly those on which the trace form is positive. -->

<a href="articles_maths/the-cone-of-positive-semidefinite-matrices-at-n-4.html">The Cone of Positive Semidefinite Matrices at $n=4$</a>
<!-- the positive semidefinite cone as the image of $B\mapsto B^{\ast}B$, closed, convex, pointed, of full dimension sixteen and self-dual for the Hilbert–Schmidt form; its faces as the subspaces, hence the Hermitian idempotents and the Grassmannians, with the extremal rays parametrised by $\mathbb{P}^{3}$; the boundary stratified by rank with dimensions $15$, $12$, $7$ and $0$; the trace sections as compact convex spectrahedra with the rank-one elements as extreme points, the cone being the cone over the section; the cone existing because the Hilbert–Schmidt form is positive definite, against the plain form $4(Q_t^{2}+B^{2})$, which is indefinite and has no cone over $\mathbb{C}$; and the real symmetric cone of dimension ten as the fixed part of the conjugation. -->

<a href="articles_maths/coda-m4c-and-the-kronecker-reading.html">Coda: $M_4(\mathbb{C})$ and the Kronecker Reading</a>
<!-- what the category established, one algebra of dimension four, one operator algebra of dimension sixteen and one matrix model of dimension sixteen, kept apart throughout; the trace form of inertia $(10,6)$ on the model, with the two halves as its eigenspaces, so that the symmetric decomposition and the form are one split read twice; the Kronecker thread $M_4(\mathbb{C})\cong M_2(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_2(\mathbb{C})$, which is $\mathbb{B}\otimes\mathbb{B}^{\mathrm{opp}}\cong\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{B})$ once the factors are named as the left and the right multiplications; every special feature of order four coming from $4=2\cdot2$; and the failure at order three, where the reading disappears, $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ is simple and the trace form has inertia $(6,3)$. -->

## Structural Comparison around Biquaternions

<!-- the eight algebras $\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{C}^{\mathrm{spl}}, \mathbb{C}^{\mathrm{dln}}, \mathbb{H}, \mathbb{H}^{\mathrm{spl}}, \mathbb{B}, \mathbb{B}^{\mathrm{spl}}$, the ladder they form and the fixed column order in which every table of this category lists them; the master table of defining data, one row per invariant and one column per algebra: the real dimension, commutativity, associativity, the division property, the zero divisors, the number of conjugations, the inertia of the norm, the minimal faithful matrix model, $\operatorname{Aut}$ and $\operatorname{Der}$, the exponential type and the topology; the conventions of the comparison tables of this category, the marker for an empty entry, and the rule that an empty entry is stated and never filled; the map from each table of the category to the article that supplies it; the place of the category at the close of Part VI and the two biquaternion systems that give it its name; the exclusion of the octonions and the reason for it. -->

<!-- the eight algebras as algebras side by side: the presentation and the defining relations; the real dimension and the centre; commutativity and associativity; the units, the zero divisors and the division property; the idempotents and the Peirce type decomposition; the ideals and the simplicity; the conjugations and the number of fixed-point subspaces; the norm, its inertia and its definiteness; the tensor-product description of the two biquaternion systems; the table of defining data and the table of algebraic properties, with a short explanation of why each property is gained or lost as the ladder from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{B}^{\mathrm{spl}}$ is climbed. -->
